title: Working the Product Settlement of a Micro Market that Settles on a Subsidy True-Up
content:
The product settlement invoiced on a subsidy true-up basis at an Unattended Micro Market Program market is the client discount met at the kiosk over the reading window, taken at the true-up share, together with the card processing charge on the shelf value of those trips, the call-out charge for unscheduled planogram work, and the fresh handling charge.

The four amounts are each rounded to the nearest cent, a figure falling exactly on the half-cent going to the nearest even cent as they are taken and are then added, and the sum is rounded the same way; none of them acts on any of the others.

The shelf value of the trips in the reading window is the discount met over that window grossed back at the share of shelf price printed against the market format and rounded to the nearest cent as it is taken, a figure falling exactly on the half-cent going to the nearest even cent; the card processing charge acts on that shelf value rather than on the discount. Where the market format's subsidy model meets no share of shelf price, no shelf value is recovered and no card processing charge is passed through.

No shortfall charge is invoiced on a subsidy true-up basis, the true-up itself already carrying what the period's trading yielded.

## The figures the calculation reads

| Figure | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Reading window | the 3 months to the day the settlement is raised |
| True-up share | the standard true-up share of 100 per cent |
| Card processing charge | the rate printed against the market format |
| Call-out charge for planogram work | none is added |
| Fresh handling charge | none is made |

## A period worked through

*Hypothetical inputs.* The client discount met at the kiosk over the three months to the day the settlement is raised totals 4200.00 USD. The market format meets a share of shelf price of 20 per cent and passes card processing through at 2.6 per cent.

The shelf value of those trips is 21000.00 USD, being 4200.00 USD grossed back at 20 per cent. The true-up is 4200.00 USD, being the discount met taken at 100 per cent. The card processing charge is 546.00 USD, being 2.6 per cent of the shelf value of 21000.00 USD. Nothing is added for planogram work and nothing for fresh handling. The four amounts added and rounded give a product settlement of 4746.00 USD.

*Hypothetical inputs, second case.* On a market format meeting no share of shelf price, no shelf value is recovered and the card processing charge is nothing; the settlement is the true-up alone.
